content: 1. Mifepristone affects the metabolism of drugs processed by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, leading to increased drug levels or effects. It is recommended to avoid or use alternative drugs in such cases. 2. Mifepristone increases the toxicity of atorvastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibitors, which may elevate the risk of myopathy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 3. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of avanafil by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Co-administration of avapritinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. 5. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. 6. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of bosentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of bromocriptine by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of budesonide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of buprenorphine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both mifepristone and buprenorphine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine in various forms (buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection) by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of calcitriol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 13. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of capmatinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of carbamazepine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, while carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of mifepristone. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of cariprazine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 16. Both ceritinib and mifepristone prolong the QTc interval. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 17. Chloramphenicol raises the levels or effects of mifepristone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 19. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of cisapride by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 20. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of clarithromycin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of colchicine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 22. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of copanlisib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of crizotinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Increased crizotinib levels may result in QT prolongation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 24. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 25. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of daridorexant by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 26. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of dasatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, consider reducing the dasatinib dose and monitor closely for adverse effects. 27. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of deflazacort by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, decrease the deflazacort dose by one-third. 28. Both desflurane and mifepristone prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 29. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of dexamethasone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of diazepam by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of disopyramide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Dofetilide increases the toxicity of mifepristone by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 33. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of dronedarone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 34. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, while efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of mifepristone. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 35. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of elacestrant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of eliglustat by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 37. Mifepristone increases the levels of eluxadoline by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID. 38. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of elvitegravir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 39. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 40. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third. 41. Both mifepristone and entrectinib prolong the QTc interval. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of entrectinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 42. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of enzalutamide by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism, while enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of mifepristone. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 43. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of erdafitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and adjust the dose accordingly. 44. Both eribulin and mifepristone prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 45. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 46. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of eszopiclone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 47. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 48. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ethosuximide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 49. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of etrasimod through mechanisms involving CYP2C9 poor metabolizers. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 50. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of everolimus by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 51. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. 52. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of felbamate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 53. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of felodipine by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 54. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of fentanyl (intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal forms) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. 55. Mifepristone decreases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 56. Both fingolimod and mifepristone prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 57. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of flurazepam by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 58. Mifepristone increases the toxicity of fluvastatin through mechanisms involving CYP2C8/2C9 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Use the smallest recommended doses for substrates and monitor for myopathy. 59. Mifepristone elevates the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 60. Mifepristone raises the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 61. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse effects. 62. Both mifepristone and givinostat prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs during initiation and concomitant use.
